svg.title: Video threads and queues
svg.desc: Video embedding uses a main thread and a separate encode and mux thread. The decode pump runs on the main thread, reads packets, sends them to FFmpeg and drains decoded frames. That thread also prepares frames and submits CUDA or OpenCL watermark work, or runs Eigen on the CPU. OpenCL hardware decoding holds two frames ahead and stages GPU copies. Owned video frames and audio or subtitle packets pass through one queue with a maximum of eight items. A full queue makes the main thread wait. The encode thread checks frame copies when needed, encodes video frames and writes all output packets. After the worker is joined, the main thread flushes the encoder and finishes the file. Detection accepts 8-bit SDR input and returns results without starting the encode thread. FFmpeg and Eigen may also use CPU worker threads.
svg.text: Two application threads during embedding, GPU engines can work on different frames
